question: Does the shipped extension keep the live broadcast selected and its volume equal to the site's own volume UI after Douyin switches a video-only player to a live stream, with no viewer gesture at all?
head: 8c644981

site.transition: A single main video element changes its MediaStream from videoTracks=1/audioTracks=0, duration=NaN, paused=true to videoTracks=1/audioTracks=1, duration=Infinity, playing. The site later mounts and removes a 10x10 finite probe video.

method: Rebuild the production extension from the recorded HEAD, load it into the specified local Chrome via CDP, sample the shipped control snapshot and the site DOM repeatedly across the transition, and keep the viewer completely passive for nine seconds after the switch. A gated smoke case asserts the automatic state before any control intent; a separate physical-oracle case guards the Huya Capture route. Two observation-only probes record the DOM shape and the shipped snapshot writes.

assertions: the site really transitioned from a video-only stream to a playing live stream
activeMedia is non-null without any gesture
live is true and volumeBase.phase is applied
volumeBase.actual equals the site's own volume number before any gesture
a later popup gesture moves element.volume, the site number and the badge together

runs.label: before repair, same HEAD before 8c644981
runs.failure: expect(state?.activeMedia).not.toBeNull() received null after a nine-second passive window

assertionsProven: The passive nine-second window leaves the shipped snapshot on the live broadcast with volumeBase 60, matching the site's own 60.
A real toolbar gesture after that passive window sets element.volume to 0.3, the site number to 30 and the badge to 30.
The Huya documentOutput/Capture route still responds to volume, mute and shortcut with a nonzero product output RMS.

observedShape.videoPhase: main video has a video-only MediaStream, duration NaN, paused true, volume 0.6, visible area 345387; several finite muted previews are registered beside it
observedShape.livePhase: the same element carries a MediaStream with an audio track, duration Infinity, playing, volume 0.6; the site volume widget reads 60 throughout
observedShape.probePlayer: a 10x10 finite video is mounted and removed a few seconds after the switch

beforeRepair.videoStage: the shipped snapshot published volumeBase 100 while the site showed 60, because a playing finite preview outranked the parked main player
beforeRepair.afterSwitch: activeMedia briefly became the tiny probe player (volumeBase 100), then the probe was removed; handleSourceReleased set activeMedia null and volumeBase phase idle
beforeRepair.stall: the content registry kept selectionVisit unchanged, so no later selected event arrived; all fourteen remaining passive samples stayed activeMedia=null / actual=null / phase=idle
beforeRepair.manualRecovery: one popup intent to 30 restored element.volume 0.3, site number 30 and badge 30

rootCause: A source release marks a retired control identity and clears activeMedia, but nothing republishes the presentation that is still on screen.
The main player's MediaStream is not counted as live presentation evidence until duration becomes Infinity, so a playing preview can win the comparison.
Before IntersectionObserver geometry arrives, a zero visibleArea is treated as invisible rather than unmeasured.
The play event picked the best of all records unconditionally instead of using the same admission rules as other lifecycle events.
repair: control-coordinator.ts: after a release clears the active source, reuse the passive view read that target changes already perform and project the still-present presentation.
media-registry.ts: count an attached MediaStream as presentation evidence alongside isLiveMedia.
media-registry.ts: fall back to the element's own layout box when recorded geometry is still zero.
media-registry.ts: route play through admitBetterCandidate instead of an unconditional best-of-all-records.
control-coordinator.spec.ts: the unit stub answers the extra passive read with capability-unavailable when no other player exists.

afterRepair.note: Every transient idle write is followed by an automatic reprojection back to media:2:1 / 60. The remaining startup projection flicker is registered as O11 and is not claimed to be eliminated.

huyaRounds.singleFailure: a live shortcut ACK timed out at volumeBase 80 while the snapshot showed 100; the first 63 assertions of that round passed and two subsequent rounds were fully green
huyaRounds.classification: real-site timing variance, not a change in the documentOutput route; the official round's RMS chain is intact
